# MyChrome

> MyChrome is a local MCP server with a native macOS app. It lets Codex, Claude Code and other local stdio MCP clients work in the Google Chrome you already use, with your existing tabs, signed-in accounts and real mouse and keyboard.

## When to use MyChrome vs. other browser tools

Use an API or web fetch first for public pages; use headless Playwright first for JavaScript pages without a login. Use MyChrome when your own Google Chrome, login or shared page matters.

## Setup and boundaries

- **Setup:** Apple Silicon, macOS 13+, Google Chrome in /Applications, native arm64 Node.js (24+ recommended; 20.19+ and 22.13+ supported), Git and Xcode Command Line Tools. Install from source with `bash scripts/setup.sh`; use `--instructions` for client connection commands. Setup does not change client configuration or grant permissions. Not published to npm.
- **Page access:** No extension, remote debugging port or separate browser profile. Page reading uses Chrome’s “Allow JavaScript from Apple Events” setting.
- **Handoff:** Name the page and authorized outcome in the original conversation. The assistant reads first and checks the result. Passwords and verification codes come back to you; explicitly say “continue”, then the assistant should reread. Continuation follows assistant instructions; MyChrome does not enforce a cross-client continuation gate.
- **Limits:** At a CAPTCHA or bot check, stop and hand over; do not solve it. On access denial or rate limits, stop and report, without switching tools to get around it. Compatibility depends on the site, account permissions and current page.
- **Control:** Ordinary physical input is intercepted during takeover. The card shows task, steps, time left and speed. Press Esc twice within 0.8 seconds to stop; another takeover needs a new instruction. Stopping does not undo sent actions. The pause control blocks input from all connections. Physical actions queue; reads can run together.
- **Pace:** Choose follow-task, key-by-key or paste input and speed from 0.5× to 3×. Optional personal input habit sampling is experimental: a 3-minute sample keeps only local timing statistics. It is not a behavioural clone and does not guarantee site acceptance.
- **Data:** Screenshots and text recognition run on the Mac. Page content returned through MCP goes to your AI client under its settings; client model charges may apply. Routine metadata recording is on by default and can be disabled; typed and selected values are not replay defaults. Local records may reveal site usage; keep them private.
- **Language:** In 0.15.0, MyChrome's windows and notifications follow your Mac's language (English or Chinese), with a Language setting under Settings in the menu bar panel.

## New in 0.15.0

- In 0.15.0, connected terminal Claude Code sessions have a read-only mirror of prompts and reply text from connection time. Thinking and tool activity are excluded. Reply in the terminal; mirror text stays in memory only. Default on; set `CHROME_BRIDGE_CLAUDE_FEED=0` in the MCP server environment and reconnect the MCP client to turn it off.
- In 0.15.0, MyChrome brings Chrome forward before acting, reports blocked input, returns the image with a text-not-ready note about 8 seconds after slow text recognition starts, and instructs assistants to use the exact open tab you requested. Reconnect to receive new instructions.
- In 0.15.0, MyChrome’s windows and notifications follow the Mac’s language (English or Chinese), with a Language setting under Settings in the menu bar panel.
